{{Short description|Method to avoid singularities in classical mechanics}}
In [[mathematical physics]], the '''Levi-Civita regularization''' is a method to transform the perturbed planar [[Kepler problem]] into a perturbed [[harmonic oscillator]] using the '''Levi-Civita (regularization) map'''. Both are named after [[Tullio Levi-Civita]], wo introduced them in 1920.

== Levi-Civita map ==
The Levi-Civita map is an extension of the real [[Hopf fibration]] <math>h_\mathbb{R}\colon S^1\rightarrow S^1</math>, using real and [[real projective space]] given by <math>h_\mathbb{R}\colon\mathbb{R}^2\supset S^1\rightarrow S^1\cong\mathbb{R}P^1,
(x,y)\mapsto[x:y]</math> or the [[complex plane]] by <math>h_\mathbb{R}\colon\mathbb{C}\supset S^1\rightarrow S^1\subset\mathbb{C},
z\mapsto z^2</math>,<ref>Waldvogel 2010, Eq. (14)</ref> by a squared radial component. It is a map <math>\Phi\colon\mathbb{C}\rightarrow\mathbb{C},
z\mapsto z^2</math> or alternatively a map <math>\Phi\colon\mathbb{R}^2\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^2</math> given by filling with <math>0\mapsto 0</math> of the map:

: <math>
h_\mathbb{R}\times-^2\colon
\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}
\cong S^1\times\mathbb{R}^+\rightarrow S^1\times\mathbb{R}^+
\cong\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}.
</math>

In [[cartesian coordinates]], the Levi-Civita map <math>\mathbb{R}^2\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^2,
(x,y)\mapsto(a,b)</math> is given by:

: <math>
a=x^2-y^2;
</math>
: <math>
b=2xy.
</math>

The above squaring of the distance, hence <math>
a^2+b^2=(x^2+y^2)^2
</math>, follows from the [[Binomial formula|binomial formulas]]. The induced map on the [[cotangent bundle]], better expressed in complex coordinates to shorten with [[complex conjugation]], is given by:

: <math>
\mathrm{d}^*\Phi\colon T^*(\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\})\rightarrow T^*(\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}),(z,w)\mapsto \left(z^2,\frac{w}{2\overline{z}}\right).
</math>

== Levi-Civita regularization ==
Let <math>
E\colon T^*(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\})\rightarrow\mathbb{R},
(q,p)\mapsto\frac{1}{2}|p|^2-\frac{1}{|q|}
</math> the [[Hamilton function]] ([[energy]]) of the [[Kepler problem]], then the Levi-Civita regularization sends it onto a common denominator:

: <math>
(E\circ\mathrm{d}^*\Phi)(p,q)
=\frac{|p|^2-8}{8|q|^2}.
</math>
